raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

With `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` fails to start at TP2 and TP4, because two AITER paths raise instead of falling back. This PR makes both fall back, as reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60021#issuecomment-6037377198. Both failures reproduce on the latest nightly, `nightly-81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93`, on both gfx942 and gfx950.

Only block-FP8 checkpoints hit either path. `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4` is unaffected: Quark leaves the n-gram embedding tables in BF16 and its MoE uses the MXFP4 path.

## Claims

* The FP8 checkpoint serves at TP2 and TP4 on MI300X with every AITER default on, and at TP4 on MI355X. Before this change it needed `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR=0`. TP2 on MI355X gets past both errors but still fails intermittently in CUDA-graph capture, for a reason unrelated to this PR (see "Known issue").
* **FP8 MoE:** `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` on its own no longer forces the AITER MoE kernel. When AITER can't serve the layer (here, block scales refined below 128x128), the oracle falls through to the next supported backend (Triton). Setting `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE` explicitly still fails loudly.
* **Custom all-reduce:** non-float tensors no longer reach AITER's custom all-reduce, whose kernel only supports float32, float16 and bfloat16. They fall back to RCCL, as with vLLM's own custom all-reduce.
* No change where AITER already worked: at TP1 both arms select AITER FP8 MoE, and float all-reduces still use AITER. GSM8K is unchanged at TP2.

## Validation

### Serving on the unmodified nightly vs. this PR

`nightly-81198e97ba`, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` at revision `236dfdf2`, MI300X:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size $TP \
    --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 256 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --trust-remote-code --reasoning-parser qwen3
```

The TP1 run used `--max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95` to fit on one GPU.

| TP | AITER settings | Without this PR | With this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | All defaults | Starts; AITER FP8 MoE | Starts; AITER FP8 MoE |
| 2 | All defaults | Fails at model init: `ValueError: FP8 MoE backend AITER does not support the deployment configuration since kernel does not support quantization scheme QuantKey(...GroupShape(row=64, col=64)...)` | Starts; Triton FP8 MoE; `Using ['AITER_CUSTOM', 'PYNCCL'] all-reduce backends` for the TP group |
| 2 | `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0` | Fails in the profile run: `custom allreduce only supports float32, float16 and bfloat16` | — (covered by all defaults) |
| 4 | All defaults | Fails at model init: same `ValueError`, with `GroupShape(row=32, col=32)` | Starts; Triton FP8 MoE |
| 4 | `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0` | Fails in the profile run: same all-reduce error | — (covered by all defaults) |

TP1 is unaffected for two reasons: the 640-wide expert dimension needs no refinement, and the n-gram embedding skips its all-reduce.

GSM8K (5-shot, chat template, all 1,319 questions) with this PR and all AITER defaults:

| TP | flexible-extract | strict-match |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | 0.9704 | 0.9712 |
| 4 | 0.9689 | 0.9697 |

The TP2 numbers equal those of the #60021 gfx942 run, where both AITER paths were disabled by hand. The server logs with this PR have no errors.

### MI355X (gfx950)

Same image, checkpoint and command:

| TP | AITER settings | Without this PR | With this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | All defaults | Fails at model init: same `ValueError`, 64x64 | Passes model init and the profile run, then a worker aborts or the engine hangs during CUDA-graph capture (most runs; see below) |
| 2 | `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0` | Fails in the profile run: same all-reduce error | — |
| 2 | `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR=0` | — | Intermittent: 1 of 4 runs started (GSM8K 0.9735 / 0.9742); the other 3 hung or aborted at the same point |
| 4 | All defaults | Fails at model init: same `ValueError`, 32x32 | Starts; GSM8K 0.9712 / 0.9719 |

The unit tests below give the same counts on gfx950. That includes the eager and CUDA-graph AITER all-reduce tests at TP2.

**Known issue, not addressed here.** With this PR, TP2 on gfx950 gets past both errors but then fails intermittently (roughly 70-80% of runs) during the real CUDA-graph capture, which follows the memory-profiling capture and the JIT kernel warmup. One worker, usually rank 1, dies with `SIGABRT` raised from `libhsa-runtime64` and no Python traceback. Less often, both ranks hang instead. The same build starts at TP2 with `--enforce-eager`, at TP4 and TP8 with AITER custom all-reduce on, and on gfx942 at TP2.

I did not find the root cause. Disabling AITER custom all-reduce (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR=0`) does not fix it: 3 of 4 runs still failed in the same place. Runs with slow capture (about 80 s or more) pass more often, so it looks timing-sensitive. The following made no difference: AITER's graph-buffer flush and IPC registration, the pinned-host n-gram weights, FLA `tensor_cache` eviction, a synchronize per capture size, `HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG`, and real versus zeroed all-reduce output in the capture warmup. The failure is independent of the two fixes in this PR, since both are exercised by the passing configurations above. It needs an AMD ROCm investigation and should be tracked separately.

### Unit tests

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fp8_tp_loading.py \
    tests/distributed/test_rocm_aiter_custom_ar.py::test_rocm_aiter_custom_allreduce
```

```text
Without this PR: 3 failed, 27 passed, 6 skipped   # exactly the new fallback cases
With this PR:    30 passed, 6 skipped             # skips are the Blackwell-only FlashInfer cases
ruff format --check / ruff check: passed
```

Both runs used image `nightly-81198e97ba`, on MI300X (gfx942) and again on MI355X (gfx950), with identical results.

* `test_fp8_aiter_falls_back_on_refined_blocks[{2-64,4-32}-False]` builds the FP8 MoE layer through the real oracle at TP2 and TP4 with only `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. It asserts the refined layout and the Triton backend.
* `test_fp8_aiter_falls_back_on_refined_blocks[...-True]` adds `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1` and asserts that the oracle still raises.
* `test_rocm_aiter_custom_allreduce[eager]` now also all-reduces an int8 tensor. It asserts that AITER declines it and that the result is still correct.

## Details

**FP8 MoE oracle.** `select_fp8_moe_backend` treated `envs.is_set("VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER")` as an explicit request for the AITER MoE kernel and called `_return_or_raise`. But `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` is AITER's global switch, and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE` defaults to on, so any user enabling AITER got a hard failure whenever the MoE kernel couldn't serve a layer.

Here that happens because the TP shard of the 640-wide expert intermediate dimension (320 at TP2, 160 at TP4) is not 128-aligned. Under `auto`, `resolve_fp8_moe_weight_block_shape` refines the scales to 64x64 or 32x32, and only Triton-based kernels accept those layouts. With this change, only an explicitly set `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE` takes the raising path. Otherwise AITER stays first in `AVAILABLE_BACKENDS`: it is still selected wherever it is supported, and the selection log shows when it was passed over.

**AITER custom all-reduce.** The Qwen4Exp n-gram embedding reduces FP8 rows as raw bytes (`embeddings.view(torch.int8)`). Each vocabulary row has one owner, so the sum is exact. `AiterCustomAllreduce.should_custom_ar` delegated to AITER's check, which doesn't look at dtype, so the tensor reached a kernel that raises. The wrapper now applies the same dtype check as `CustomAllreduce.should_custom_ar`, and `CudaCommunicator.all_reduce` moves on to the next backend (PyNCCL/RCCL). Float inputs are unaffected.

**Scope.** Neither change is architecture-specific. Both were validated on gfx942 and gfx950. TP8 is out of scope: there the 80-wide shard is too small to refine, and `Fp8MoEMethod.create_weights` rejects it (`output_size ... = 80 is not divisible by weight quantization block_n = 128`) before either AITER path is reached.

**Trade-off.** On these configurations the MoE runs on Triton rather than AITER, which is what users get today by disabling AITER MoE by hand. Letting AITER serve these layers would need either padded TP shards that keep 128x128 blocks (as `pad_tp_shard_to_weight_blocks` already does for an explicit `--moe-backend`) or smaller-block support in AITER. Both are out of scope here.

Co-authored-by: Cursor

files.patch:
@@ -119,6 +119,13 @@ def eager_allreduce(
             out = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(inp)
             torch.testing.assert_close(out, expected)
 
+        # Raw FP8 bytes are reduced as int8, which AITER's kernel rejects.
+        inp = torch.ones((2, 7168), dtype=torch.int8, device=device)
+        aiter_ar_comm = get_tp_group().device_communicator.aiter_ar_comm
+        assert not aiter_ar_comm.should_custom_ar(inp)
+        out = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(inp)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out, inp * tp_size)
+
 
 @pytest.mark.skipif(not is_aiter_found(), reason="AITER is not installed")
 @multi_gpu_test(num_gpus=2)

@@ -309,3 +309,36 @@ def test_fp8_block_aligned_tp_flashinfer_matches_unsharded(
             f"unsharded_fi_vs_triton_l2={cross_backend_l2.item():.6f}"
         )
         assert relative_l2 < 0.01, relative_l2.item()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("explicit_aiter_moe", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tp_size,block", [(2, 64), (4, 32)])
+def test_fp8_aiter_falls_back_on_refined_blocks(
+    monkeypatch, default_vllm_config, tp_size, block, explicit_aiter_moe
+):
+    """A TP shard that is not 128-aligned refines the 128x128 checkpoint
+    blocks, which AITER's FP8 MoE does not support. VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER alone
+    must fall back to another backend; only an explicit
+    VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE may raise.
+    """
+    from vllm._aiter_ops import is_aiter_found_and_supported, rocm_aiter_ops
+    from vllm.envs import disable_envs_cache
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.oracle.fp8 import Fp8MoeBackend
+
+    if not is_aiter_found_and_supported():
+        pytest.skip("Requires ROCm with AITER")
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER", "1")
+    if explicit_aiter_moe:
+        monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE", "1")
+    else:
+        monkeypatch.delenv("VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE", raising=False)
+    disable_envs_cache()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(rocm_aiter_ops, "is_fused_moe_enabled", lambda: True)
+
+    if explicit_aiter_moe:
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="FP8 MoE backend AITER"):
+            _make_fp8_tp_experts(monkeypatch, tp_size, 0, "auto", mock_backend=False)
+        return
+    layer = _make_fp8_tp_experts(monkeypatch, tp_size, 0, "auto", mock_backend=False)
+    assert layer.quant_method.moe_block_shape == [block, block]
+    assert layer.quant_method.fp8_backend == Fp8MoeBackend.TRITON
